criteria.rationale: The defining risk for AI drafting software is whether output is accurate enough to keep firms paying when cheaper tools do the same job. The founders name model errors and GST-data dependence as risks, but they give no accuracy data and push responsibility to the CA. The deck has a material contradiction with the form on customers: 31 'paying' firms vs 24 paying plus 7 on trial. The deck also labels MRR x 12 as ARR and claims no competitor offers AI notice replies, which the web contradicts. Together these weigh on candour.

gates.detail: Checked all 88 portfolio companies; none sells GST reconciliation or notice drafting to CA firms. Nearest adjacencies: Sketchnote (startup operating system; customer is startups, not CA firms), EximFiles (shipment documents), CommandK (DPDP/GDPR compliance for tech companies), Nawgati (compliance SaaS for fuel stations), GloRoots (EOR/payroll), Medmitra (AI decision support for doctors: vertical-AI analogue, different industry). Different customer or different job in each case.

The model does not depend on a withdrawn or pending permission. Access to GST data runs through the standard GSP/ASP ecosystem, which is a path-to-market question scored under R4, not a rule-change dependency.

The founders selected 'Fintech', but there is no money movement or lending. This is B2B vertical AI/SaaS for CA firms, so the fintech label is a stretch. The genuine fit is the Indian vertical-AI focus (scored under S1). Flag only.
Pre-seed, INR 1.5 Cr at INR 10 Cr post-money, one angel. Within the lead mandate.

case_for: A practising CA who lived this problem built the product. It has 24 paying firms with MRR up about 4x in three months, through referrals rather than paid acquisition (S3, R3).
Vertical AI for one industry, capital-light, and a small first round the fund can lead (S1, R5, S2).
The founders name model errors and GST-data dependence as risks (R1).
case_against: The deck counts 7 free-trial firms as paying (31 vs 24), labels MRR x 12 as ARR, and claims no competitor offers AI notice replies. These contradictions on customers and competition weigh on candour (R1).
Cheaper tools already do the same job (GST Reply AI at INR 999 a month unlimited; Vyapar TaxOne reconciliation), and the founders do not acknowledge them (R4, R6, S4).
Distribution so far is the CEO's personal network; no retention cohorts, trial conversion or accuracy data (R3, R6).
Liability is pushed to the CA, and the GST data access route is undescribed (R1, R4).
call_questions: Your deck says 31 paying firms and the form says 24 paying plus 7 on trial. Which is right, and why the difference? (Pressure test: we are watching how you respond to the discrepancy.)
Of firms that started paying in August, how many still pay and at what MRR? What share of trials convert?
What share of drafted replies are filed with minimal edits, and what is the false-match rate in reconciliation?
Why would a firm pay INR 2,500-6,000 a month for CAPilot when GST Reply AI offers unlimited replies at INR 999 a month?
Do you pull GST data through a GSP API or manual uploads, and how do you protect client tax data?
How many paying firms have come from outside your personal CA network?
what_would_change_our_view: Consistent customer reporting, plus cohort retention and accuracy data showing firms outside the founders' network stay and pay above cheaper alternatives.
